div.head: VI Atr 37
div.ab: K. ⁊ gyf hwa ymbe cyninges feorh syrwe, sy he his feores scyldig ⁊ ealles þæs þe he age, gif hit him ongesoþod weorðe; ⁊ gif he hine ladian wille ⁊ mage, do þæt be þam deopestan aðe oþþe mid þryfealdan ordale on Ængla lage, ⁊ on Dena lage be þam þe heora lagu sy.

⁊ gyf hwa ymbe cyninges feorh syrwe, sy he his feores scyldig ⁊ ealles þæs þe he age, gif hit him ongesoþod weorðe; ⁊ gif he hine ladian wille ⁊ mage, do þæt be þam deopestan aðe oþþe mid þryfealdan ordale on Ængla lage, ⁊ on Dena lage be þam þe heora lagu sy.

And gyf hwa ymbe cyninges feorh syrwe, sy he his feores scyldig and ealles þæs þe he age gif hit him ongesoþod weorðe; and gif he hine ladian wille and mage, do þæt be þam deopestan aðe oþþe mid þryfealdan ordale on Ængla lage, and on Dena lage be þam þe heora lagu sy.

Und wenn jemand nach dem Leben des Königs trachtet, sei er [des Verlustes] seines Lebens schuldig und alles dessen, was er besitzt, wenn es ihm nachgewiesen wird; und wenn er sich reinigen will und kann, thue er das durch den schwersten Eid oder durch dreifaches Ordal im Engländerrecht und im Dänenrecht gemäss dem, was deren Recht ist.

And if anyone plots against the king's life, let him be liable [to lose] his life and all that he owns, if it is proved against him; and if he wishes and is able to clear himself, let him do it by the heaviest oath or by the threefold ordeal under English law, and under Danish law according to what their law is.

And if anyone plots against the king’s life, he shall forfeit his life and all that he possesses, if it is proved against him; and if he seeks and is able to clear himself, he shall do so by means of the most solemn oath or by the triple ordeal in districts under English law, and in those under Danish law in accordance with their constitution.

And if anyone conspires against the king’s life, his life and all that he owns will be forfeit if he is shown to be guilty; and if he wishes to exonerate himself and is granted permission, he can do so with the most serious oath or with the threefold ordeal under English law, and in the Danelaw according to their legal customs.

Steenstrup Danelag 226 vermutet hinter dem nicht genannten Beweismittel den Zweikampf (s. d. Gl 5), den er als besonders Dänische Reinigung erweist aus Hincmars Bericht vom Dänen, der in Frankreich 863 eine Anklage auf infidelitatem beweist secundum gentis sue morem cum eo negante armis coram rege contendens, ed. Mon. Germ., SS. I 462. Ein Personalrecht (s. d. Gl) seh ich aber nicht hierin, sondern territorialisiertes Partikularrecht der Denalagu; s. d. Gl 1b. 11j

Steenstrup Danelag 226 supposes that behind the unnamed means of proof lies judicial combat (see that word in Gl 5), which he shows to be a specifically Danish mode of clearing oneself from Hincmar’s report of the Dane who in France in 863 proves an accusation of infidelitatem secundum gentis sue morem cum eo negante armis coram rege contendens, ed. Mon. Germ., SS. I 462. I, however, see in this not a personal law (see that word in Gl), but the territorialized particular law of the Denalagu; see that word in Gl 1b. 11j
Cf. V, 30 and note. The Latin version reads: nisi forte maximo iuramento vel fervente ferro excusetur. It has no mention of the Danelaw.
Steenstrup (Danelag, p. 226) suggests that clearing by holmgang, i.e. ‘duel,’ is meant.
